title: AKI Staging & Renal Replacement Therapy
sources: Critical Vector — ICU Pocket Guide: AKI Staging & RRT
KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury (2012)

changelog.change: Initial entry — KDIGO staging, the nephrotoxin list, the AEIOU emergent-RRT indications, and default CRRT settings.

summary: Stage AKI on whichever is worse — creatinine or urine output. Stop nephrotoxins, optimise volume and perfusion, and dose-adjust drugs. Start RRT emergently for the AEIOU indications; timing of RRT for AKI without an emergent indication is not improved by starting early (STARRT-AKI, AKIKI).

body.text: KDIGO staging (use the worse of the two)

rows: ↑ ≥ 0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, OR ↑ 1.5–1.9× baseline within 7 days
↑ ≥ 3× baseline, OR ≥ 4.0 mg/dL, OR RRT started, OR (< 18 y) eGFR < 35
< 0.3 mL/kg/h for ≥ 24 h, OR anuria ≥ 12 h

body.text: Avoid nephrotoxins: NSAIDs, iodinated contrast (see the contrast-associated-AKI module), aminoglycosides, vancomycin without AUC monitoring, and stop / renally dose ACE-I/ARB, metformin (contrast), and SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness. Check drug doses against the current eGFR — and remember creatinine LAGS a falling GFR.

rows: Severe metabolic acidosis (pH < 7.1) refractory to bicarbonate / respiratory compensation
K⁺ > 6.5 mEq/L refractory to medical therapy (or rapidly rising with ECG changes)
A dialysable toxin: methanol, ethylene glycol, lithium, salicylate, valproic acid, metformin (with lactic acidosis)
Fluid overload (≈ ≥ 10% body weight) refractory to diuretics, causing hypoxaemia
BUN > 100 with uraemic symptoms — pericarditis / rub, encephalopathy / asterixis, uraemic bleeding

body.text: Without an AEIOU emergency, a watchful-waiting strategy (start RRT when an indication develops) is non-inferior to early elective initiation and avoids RRT altogether in a substantial fraction of patients (AKIKI, IDEAL-ICU, STARRT-AKI).

items: Mode: CVVHDF (convection + diffusion) is the common default; CVVH or CVVHD are equivalent for solute clearance.

Dose: effluent 20–25 mL/kg/h prescribed (prescribe ~25–30 to allow for downtime and achieve the delivered target). Higher-intensity dosing has no outcome benefit and worsens micronutrient / antibiotic clearance.

Anticoagulation: regional citrate is first-line (longer filter life, less bleeding) — contraindicated / cautious in severe liver failure or shock with lactic acidosis (citrate accumulation → rising total:ionised calcium ratio). Systemic UFH is the alternative; no anticoagulation if actively bleeding.
Protein: 2.0–2.5 g/kg/day on CRRT (amino acid losses across the filter). Watch for hypophosphataemia and hypokalaemia — often need to add phosphate / potassium to the replacement fluid.
Re-dose antibiotics for CRRT clearance (e.g. higher β-lactam doses, vancomycin by levels) — under-dosing is common.

buildNote: Tier 3. STARRT-AKI / AKIKI timing evidence added from standard practice. A contrast-nephropathy pathway already exists as its own module.
